title: So proud of them!!! #nyc #arts #experience #timesquare
transcript: If you happen to be in Times Square at just the right time, you could see something really cool and delightfully strange. The ads on the screens disappear, taken over by an art project spanning the entire square. This is a curated series organized by Times Square Arts, which they've been doing since 2012, and there's a new artist featured every month, but this month holds a really special significance for me personally. The project featured through the entire month of September was actually created by my cousin Bow and their partner Liz. And together as a performance art duo, they're known as LIZN’BOW Continuing their ongoing Niña Project, which blends an eye-popping, childlike fantasy aesthetic with Reggaeton performance. And for three minutes every night, they turn Times Square into Niñalandia. This week I attended their launch Celebration alongside friends, colleagues and collaborators, after which Times Square Arts blocked off the iconic red steps and turned it into our private platform for a joyous viewing. Also, mark your calendars because on September 23rd, they're doing a one night only concert performance leading up to the display. I've seen them perform before and it's a really fun kooky time. But in either case, if you're tired of seeing the Times Square screens used only for ads, you should definitely check out this ongoing series. It's called The Midnight Moment and it lasts three minutes starting at 11:57 PM every night until midnight.
classificationReason: Content about a Times Square public art installation by the creator's cousin — not related to any stage production.
